issues.description: check_road_link_reciprocity() exempted any reciprocal link whose elementType != "road" as junction-mediated with no check that the named junction actually connects the two roads (dangling/unrelated junction ids were silently exempt); first tightening (8f22c704) required a backing <connection>, but a <connection> never names the exit-side road B, so every genuine one-way junction exit (22588 of 45176 road-road links on the real 07_lanes map) was flagged as a false violation; final tightening (ed1bd069, 8c4424f0) requires road@junction==J for the connecting side and checks exit-side backing without requiring B to appear in a <connection>.
issues.residual_risk: On the real 07_lanes map (sha256 787870ba..., read-only per 8c4424f0's commit message) gated violations = 0. See GAP-070 for the separate, still-open reference-line geometry finding this work surfaced.

issues.subsystem: map geometry (junction connector exits) -- real 07_lanes map
issues.description: While validating GAP-069's structural fix, 8c4424f0 added a separate geometry check: the reference-line gap between a junction connecting road's touching end and its exit road's touching end must not exceed the combined carriageway width. 4370 of 4577 real junction exits meet this (500/500 randomly paired unrelated roads correctly rejected), but 207 exits sit 3.5-7 m beyond the combined carriageway width at the reference line. This is reported as junction_exit_geometry_gap (NOT gated), because gating would block every run on what is a pre-existing map-geometry defect, and widening the tolerance to pass them is explicitly not permitted (GAP-026 is never fixed by raising tolerance).
issues.regression_test: ultimate_pipeline/tests/unit/test_check_road_link_reciprocity.py (covers the structural/geometry split, not the 207 real-map exits themselves)
issues.residual_risk: Likely the same connector-geometry class already tracked as GAP-026 (MAP_DEFECT_CONFIRMED, per prior closure); needs a source-stage geometry fix at the connector-generation stage, not a tolerance change, and not a final-XODR cosmetic mutation. Not fixed in this remediation window.

issues.description: ValidationReport.add(self, level, stage, message) is called with the arguments reversed, i.e. add(stage, "error", message), at approximately 9 older call sites across pipeline_stages. Because level is the first parameter, these calls record level=<stage name> and stage="error", so the intended error-level entries land classified as whatever level string the stage name happens to be read as, not as errors -- in practice they end up filed as warnings rather than errors. Confirmed call sites: stage_04_enrichment.py:259,341,362,395; stage_08_integrity.py:814; stage_09_positional_semantics.py:237,257,290,304; stage_12_domain_gap.py:322 (9 sites, verified by grep on 2026-11-03).
issues.residual_risk: Fixing this changes run outcomes (entries move from warnings into errors, which can flip pass/fail gates), so 8c4424f0's commit message explicitly deferred it as a separate change needing its own assessment rather than a drive-by fix. Still open as of 2026-11-03.

issues.description: OSM way/node identity is lost in the OSM->XODR conversion path: ultimate_pipeline/enrichment/osm_meta_index.py documents in-repo that XODR road ids are Osm2Odr/netconvert-assigned sequence numbers, not OSM way ids, so lane successor/predecessor topology built on XODR ids cannot be cross-checked against OSM directly. netconvert's --output.original-names flag is available to carry original OSM way ids through the conversion but is not currently used in this pipeline's conversion invocation.
issues.residual_risk: Needs an operator decision: wire --output.original-names (or equivalent id-carrying mechanism) through the conversion and re-verify lane-link topology against real OSM ids, or formally document that successor/predecessor topology is XODR-internal-id-only and not OSM-traceable. Not attempted in this remediation window (source-stage-only fix, no cosmetic XODR mutation permitted as a substitute).
